hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $-1$.
And the point at $-1$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **less than $-1$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 1 and continues left. An open point is plotted at negative 1 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x \leq -1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 1 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at negative 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/175f0c9151882553a4be9ed80682e7f1538f7ef1)

The graph of $x > -1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 1 and continues right. An open point is plotted at negative 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6cb0017a77a27610e1b9255c8f26a339db58f50d)

The graph of $x \geq -1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 1 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at negative 1 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/490e0d6489782fef935b8e7936484fb7ca874a7f)
